remaining_concerns: Current admissible evidence shows the enterprise refund-workflow slice is 1.8 percentage points below the warning threshold in a named launch use case.
No current-release documentation was provided showing that this material weakness is disclosed in the certification materials.
No approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance was provided for the refund-workflow regression.
The release thread contains only an informal monitoring comment, which policy says cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
Prior approval is only contextual because it predates the current prompt-template change and current evaluation batch.

Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall readiness but do not satisfy the separate policy predicate requiring disclosure or approved mitigation for material segment weaknesses.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor presented no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position to a caveated interpretation of the same record. That reframing is not enough to move the result to compliant_with_caveats here, because the caveat is not merely a disclosure note on an otherwise satisfied record; it is the unresolved compliance predicate itself. The governing policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation before certification may proceed. The available evidence shows a current refund-workflow subgroup regression, plus the absence of attached reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language. The Actor expressly concedes those points and does not dispute that the record does not support unqualified compliance. Aggregate readiness, clean rehearsal results, public governance principles, and prior approval context may support general release readiness, but they do not cure the unmet certification requirement on the present record.
